- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days), suggesting a bias toward higher values.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 90s to 97s), model forecasts overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly — exhibit lagged mean reversion.
- Forecasts tend to plateau or rise slowly after a peak, while true prices often drop or stabilize earlier — model underreacts to volatility.
- In low-price regimes (e.g., 80s), model forecasts remain elevated, suggesting failure to recognize mean reversion or downward momentum.
- Model shows poor sensitivity to recent price drops — fails to adjust forecast downward when true prices fall sharply (e.g., 89.32 → 82.26).
- Forecasts often lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in downward trends — model is slow to react to new information.
- In multi-day price corrections, model tends to smooth out volatility, underestimating magnitude of drops or overestimating recovery speed.
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent highs” — forecasts remain high even when history shows downward drift or consolidation.
